title: R6B district - maximum residential floor area ratio with qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing (ZR 23-22 second column), computed as a separately labeled alternative
description: DRAFT extraction (needs_review) that COMPUTES the ZR 23-22 qualifying-housing allowance for R6B: qualifying_max_residential_far (2.40) and qualifying_max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft (lot area x 2.40). It is the second of two separately labeled R6B allowances: the standard allowance (2.00, max_residential_far / max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft) stays with rule r6-r12-residential-far, unchanged. This rule lives in its own family (residential_far_qualifying_housing) so no consumer of the residential_far family can mistake the alternative for the standard allowance, and so no other district's result changes. R6B has no wide-street increase. Whether a development contains qualifying affordable or qualifying senior housing is a separate legal determination this rule never makes: when housing_program is standard_residence the alternative is not applicable; when it is absent or qualifying, the alternative is computed and labeled conditional. NOT a Verified determination. Behind the lane A flag (lane_flag A): indexed only when LANE_A_ENABLED is on.

citations.quote: Separate maximum #residential# #floor area ratios# are set forth for #zoning lots# containing standard #residences# and #zoning lots# containing #qualifying affordable housing# or #qualifying senior housing#.

inputs.name: zoning_district
inputs.description: Residence district governing the lot. Scope is enforced by applicability (R6B only), not an input enum: any other district is a visible not_applicable.

inputs.name: lot_area_sq_ft
inputs.description: Zoning-lot area in square feet; must be strictly positive. A zero/negative/non-finite value is rejected fail-closed (professional_review_required, no computed value).

inputs.name: housing_program
inputs.description: Same vocabulary as r6-r12-residential-far. standard_residence -> this alternative is not applicable (visible not_applicable). Absent, qualifying_affordable_housing or qualifying_senior_housing -> the alternative is computed and labeled conditional; qualification itself is never decided here.

outputs.name: qualifying_max_residential_far
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area ratio for zoning lots containing qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing (ZR 23-22 second column).

outputs.name: qualifying_max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area with qualifying affordable or qualifying senior housing = lot area x qualifying_max_residential_far.

parameters.name: qualifying_far_by_district
parameters.note: ZR 23-22 table, R6B row, 'Qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing' column: 2.40 (standard column 2.00, which rule r6-r12-residential-far computes). Keys equal the applicability set.

steps.note: Select the qualifying affordable / senior housing maximum residential FAR for the district (ZR 23-22 second column).
Maximum residential floor area with qualifying housing = lot area (sq ft) x qualifying FAR.

exceptions.description: This allowance applies only to zoning lots containing qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing (ZR 23-22 second column). It is an alternative beside the standard-residences allowance of rule r6-r12-residential-far (max_residential_far / max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft), never a replacement: whether a development qualifies is a separate legal determination not made by this rule.

R6B has no wide-street increase: in the ZR 23-22 table R6B appears in exactly one row and carries no footnote marker (footnote 1 is the 'within 100 feet of a wide street' condition), so neither the standard 2.00 nor the qualifying 2.40 changes with street width. The wide-street-conditional rule r6-r7-r8-wide-street-conditional-far covers only R6, R7-1, R7-2 and R8.

special_district_interactions.description: Special Purpose Districts (ZR Articles VIII-XIV) and other mapped overlays may modify residence-district floor area. When a mapped special district applies, its provisions govern and must be evaluated by the corresponding special rule; this rule does not apply the modification.

uncertainty_policy.note: An uncertain, split, sliver, or invalid M2-T013 geometric district assignment is never collapsed into a single definitive district: coverage is downgraded to professional_review_required (or data_conflict) and the geometric uncertainty is recorded in the trace.

limitations: Draft extraction pending independent review and G6 qualified-human legal approval; not a Verified determination.
Only R6B is computed; the qualifying column of every other ZR 23-22 district stays surfaced (not computed) by its existing rule.
Whether a development qualifies (qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing, and any related unit or income requirements) is not evaluated.
Special Purpose District and other overlay modifications are not applied.
